phase_name: Permission Broker Production Consumption Independent Implementation Verification
summary: Independent implementation verification of Phase 148E's PBPC-001 v1.2 production consumption wiring in pcae push -- verification only, no src/pcae/** or docs/contracts/** modification (both confirmed empty via git diff --name-only HEAD -- src/pcae/ and -- docs/contracts/). Reconstructed the production diff independently (git diff 21a35087..5b015852 -- src/: exactly one file, src/pcae/commands/push.py, +166/-0, sole-production-file claim confirmed; permission_broker_foundation.py and permission_broker.py diffs both empty). Independently searched the entire src/pcae tree (AST-based, not trusting the claimed count of two) for every git-push dispatch mechanism: found five real dispatch sites total -- the two inside push.py (run_push/_run_push_staged_file_aware, both broker-gated) plus three pre-existing, unrelated, ungated sites (core/agent.py's Phase 42E push_file_changes, reachable only via pcae agent; commands/phase.py's two historical one-off push-execution commands, reachable only via distinct pcae phase ... subcommands with their own approval flags) -- none of the three are reachable through the pcae push CLI verb, so all fall outside PBPC-001's stated pcae-push-only MVP scope; recorded as Observation F-148F-2, not Blocking. Traced run_push() and _run_push_staged_file_aware() line-by-line: confirmed the Decision Consumption Point is evaluated exactly once per attempt, strictly before the sole git push subprocess.run call on each path, with no branch, fallback, or error-recovery path bypassing it. Independently re-verified the canonical request shape, field-by-field, directly from the adapter body (not 148E's tests): action_type=push, execution_class=mutation (hardcoded, no CLI/env override surface), requested_component=COMP-001, requested_capability=pcae_push, approval_present=False (hardcoded), simulation_only=True (hardcoded, independently re-confirmed load-bearing via a fresh POL-005 DENY control with simulation_only=False), task_id sourced from find_latest_active_task with no fabricated fallback. Independently re-derived POL-004 non-applicability to execution_class=mutation directly from MissingHumanApprovalRule's applicable_execution_classes set. Wrote and ran a new independent adversarial test suite (tests/test_phase_148f_permission_broker_production_consumption_independent_verification.py, 11 tests, no production file touched) covering: repository-wide dispatch-site inventory assertion; a duck-typed fake-ALLOW object (broader than 148E's plain-string invalid-result test) rejected on both paths; Permission Broker CONSTRUCTION failure (distinct from 148E's evaluate()-failure test) -- discovered this is NOT wrapped in the adapter's try/except and propagates as an uncaught exception out of pcae.cli.main() itself (Finding F-148F-1, Non-Blocking: no dispatch occurs either way, but the failure is not diagnostically graceful); the reverse stale-decision sequence (DENY then genuine ALLOW), proving no stale denial is cached either, complementing 148E's ALLOW-then-DENY-only test; an independent Permission Broker consumer-scope inventory (repository-wide, classifying all five consumer files, confirming commit.py/task.py/phase.py remain unwired); a mechanical-block-cannot-be-overridden-by-a-genuine-ALLOW case (force-push-required, with a real forced ALLOW decision, confirming the broker is not even constructed for that attempt); and an independent HARD_BLOCK_REGISTRY recount (12, unchanged). All 11 pass. Also identified, by direct contract re-reading, that PBPC-001 v1.2 Section 17 (PBPC-REQ-059/060/061, Final Pre-Dispatch Validation / re-observation of HEAD/branch/unpushed-count/task-ID immediately before dispatch) is not implemented anywhere in the adapter or either dispatch site (Finding F-148F-3, Non-Blocking: the gap between decision and dispatch is a handful of synchronous statements with no intervening I/O under the single-agent-lock model; concurrent-process races are separately out-of-scope per PBPC-REQ-055; no exploit was constructed). Independently re-ran the full regression battery: combined push/148F suite (143 passed), two additional push suites discovered by independent search (test_commit_push_preflight.py/test_commit_push_preflight_review.py, 74 passed), Permission Broker Foundation/applicability/composition/rule-framework/148C.7/148C.8 suites (333 passed), broker/CLI/command-path/observation suites (551 passed), Runtime context/introspection/snapshot/contract suites (903 passed), 148F's own suite standalone (11 passed), and fast_green (4391 passed, 0 failed, unchanged from 148D/148E's reported baseline -- 148F's new suite is slow/integration-marked and excluded from that count by design). Zero Blocking findings; two Non-Blocking findings (F-148F-1, F-148F-3) and one Observation (F-148F-2), all recommended for a future bounded repair/tracking phase, none deferred silently. 148C-B-1 remains CLOSED (independently re-confirmed, not re-adjudicated); PBPC-001 remains v1.2; PBPA-001 remains v1.0, unamended; runtime remains Observed/observe/unavailable; Prompt Generation (Phase 45F) remains DEFERRED STRATEGIC OBSERVATION, untouched. Verdict: VERIFIED WITH NON-BLOCKING FINDINGS -- PBPC-001 v1.2 PRODUCTION CONSUMPTION CONFORMS. See docs/PHASE_148F_PERMISSION_BROKER_PRODUCTION_CONSUMPTION_INDEPENDENT_IMPLEMENTATION_VERIFICATION.md for full detail.
